## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
According to SuttaCentral, passage-level parallels exist with the *Ñāṇakathā* of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1), and related expositions occur in the *Mahāsatipaṭṭhānasutta* (DN 22) and the *Jarāsuttaniddesa* (Mnd 6) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse across 269 texts, with its most substantial alignments occurring in DN 22 (§14.4–50.2 ↔ §18.44–21.26), other chapters of the *Vibhaṅga* (including the *Dhātuvibhaṅga*, *Maggaṅgavibhaṅga*, and *Āyatanavibhaṅga*), and the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1, §2.0–26.1 ↔ §179.1_2–193.30) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus records automated cross-language correspondences with Sanskrit texts including the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, the Sarvāstivāda *Dharmaskandha*, the *Śrāvakabhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, the *Daśasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā*, the Chinese *Madhyama-āgama* (T 26), and Tibetan translations such as the *Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya* (D 3897) and Śamathadeva's *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* (D 4094) [DharmaNexus].

- Passage-level parallels (SuttaCentral): Ps 1.1 Ñāṇakathā
